text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- All suggested changes to the Zimbabwe constitution, including the reintroduction of a two-chamber legislature, can be considered and adopted if there is support, but these suggestions must be approved first by the southern African country's ruling ZANU-PF party before going to parliament, President Robert Mugabe said.
Mugabe's party is under pressure to consider wide-ranging changes to a constitution which critics say has been designed to entrench its power hold since it assumed office over 16 years ago.

- The government Public Service Commission (PSC) said some 600 state nurses and doctors who want to end a six-week strike for higher wages must await individual letters accepting their return to work, PSC officials said on Monday.
Officials say many of the 10,000 nurses and doctors who started the strike had returned to work over the past month.
